about: Named cameras that reproduce a specific rendering fault, so a check is a name rather than four numbers pasted from a screenshot. `bash shot.sh <tag> --spot <name>` warps here and captures the GL/Vulkan pair.

dbab02-flatswap.shows: A lava floor in the fire corridor that renders as a completely different flat -- green foliage on orange -- in the Vulkan backend and correctly in GL. Reported as 'the triangulation isn't working and random textures get filled-in'; it is the animated-texture re-resolve repainting a batch that merged two different base textures.
dbab02-flatswap.correct: The floor is dark red lava with bright yellow veins, matching GL.

dbab02-missinggrate.shows: A metal grate 3D floor spanning a lava pit. GL draws the grate and its side beams; Vulkan draws nothing at all and you see straight down to the lava. It comes and goes as the view turns, so it is a coverage problem, not a shading one.
dbab02-missinggrate.correct: The grate and the beams between its top and bottom planes are present, as in GL.

dbab01-glassfloor.shows: Looking down into the lava pit at a translucent 3D floor. The grate reads as more solid in Vulkan than in GL.
dbab01-glassfloor.correct: The lava beneath shows through at the same strength as GL, and a pickup lying on the floor sits on it rather than through it.
